prompt:
Given several related papers, compare mechanisms, scaling behavior, memory or retrieval behavior, failure modes, and which design choice should be used in a real research-agent system.

Paper: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
Core idea: Interleave reasoning traces with actions so the model can plan, call tools, observe results, and update its trajectory.
Known risks: depends on tool availability, prompted trajectories can be brittle

Paper: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
Core idea: Teaches a language model to decide when and how to call external tools by generating and filtering its own tool-use examples.
Known risks: tool quality and API design matter, bad tool calls can degrade output, requires filtering useful annotations

Paper: Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs
Core idea: Teach an LLM to call APIs accurately by grounding generation in retrieved API documentation and tool-specific training data.
Known risks: API changes require refreshed documentation, tool-call correctness needs strict validation

Paper: AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation
Core idea: Compose multiple customizable LLM agents that converse with each other, tools, code, and humans to solve complex tasks.
Known risks: orchestration complexity, quality depends on agent role design and model reliability

Paper: The Fugu Framework: An Open-Ended and Adaptive Framework for Collaborative AI Agents
Core idea: An adaptive framework for coordinating collaborative AI agents and constructing task-specific agentic workflows.
Known risks: workflow brittleness, cost and latency, verification burden

Paper: Phi-3 Technical Report: A Highly Capable Language Model Locally on Your Phone
Core idea: Shows that small language models can be highly capable when trained on carefully filtered and synthetic data.
Known risks: capacity ceiling versus large models, synthetic-data bias risk, architecture novelty is mostly in recipe and variants

Paper: MobileBERT: a Compact Task-Agnostic BERT for Resource-Limited Devices
Core idea: Compress BERT into a mobile-friendly encoder using bottleneck architecture and task-agnostic distillation from a larger teacher.
Known risks: encoder-only, teacher quality bounds student quality

Paper: DistilBERT, a distilled version of BERT: smaller, faster, cheaper and lighter
Core idea: Reduce BERT size and latency by distilling a smaller encoder that preserves much of the teacher's language understanding ability.
Known risks: less capacity than full BERT, inherits teacher biases and limitations

Paper: Gemma 2: Improving Open Language Models at a Practical Size
Core idea: Improves practical open models with local-global attention, grouped-query attention, and distillation for smaller sizes.
Known risks: not a frontier-scale model, local attention can limit far-context mixing, distillation depends on teacher quality

sources.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
sources.core_idea: A selective state-space model that makes SSM parameters input-dependent and uses hardware-aware scan for efficient long-sequence modeling.

sources.title: Retentive Network: A Successor to Transformer for Large Language Models
sources.core_idea: A retention-based architecture designed to combine parallel training with recurrent-style inference for efficient long-sequence modeling.

prompt:
Design ablations, baselines, failure probes, and measurable benchmarks that would prove whether the proposed architecture is useful.

Paper: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
Core idea: Manage limited context windows like an operating system by teaching an LLM agent to page information between working and archival memory.
Known risks: memory policies can fail, requires reliable self-management

Paper: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
Core idea: Teach a language model to decide when to retrieve, use retrieved evidence, and critique its own grounded outputs.
Known risks: requires specialized training data, reflection signals can be brittle

Paper: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
Core idea: Interleave reasoning traces with actions so the model can plan, call tools, observe results, and update its trajectory.
Known risks: depends on tool availability, prompted trajectories can be brittle

Paper: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
Core idea: A modern MoE LLM using multi-head latent attention, sparse experts, and multi-token prediction for efficient large-scale training and inference.
Known risks: complex large-scale engineering, routing stability, precision and infrastructure sensitivity

Paper: Command R: Retrieval-Augmented Generation at Production Scale
Core idea: Specialize a language model for enterprise retrieval and tool-using workflows where citations and grounded context matter.
Known risks: architecture details are less fully specified than open research papers, quality depends on retriever and corpus

Paper: Mixtral of Experts
Core idea: Extends Mistral-style dense Transformers with token-level sparse expert routing to increase capacity while keeping active compute lower.
Known risks: routing load balance complexity, expert specialization is hard to inspect, serving requires expert-aware infrastructure

Paper: Jamba: A Hybrid Transformer-Mamba Language Model
Core idea: Interleave attention, Mamba state-space layers, and sparse experts to gain long-context efficiency without abandoning Transformer strengths.
Known risks: many interacting design choices, harder ablation surface than pure backbones

Paper: LLM-JEPA: Large Language Models Meet Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures
Core idea: Applies JEPA-style embedding-space prediction to language-model learning, shifting part of the objective from token reconstruction to latent prediction.
Known risks: latent usefulness must be validated downstream, harder evaluation than token loss, objective design sensitivity

Paper: The Fugu Framework: An Open-Ended and Adaptive Framework for Collaborative AI Agents
Core idea: An adaptive framework for coordinating collaborative AI agents and constructing task-specific agentic workflows.
Known risks: workflow brittleness, cost and latency, verification burden

Paper: LFM2 Technical Report: Efficient Mobile Foundation Models
Core idea: An efficient mobile foundation-model design using hardware-aware hybrid layers with short convolutions and a smaller number of attention/GQA blocks.
Known risks: may trade off raw capacity, hardware-specific design choices, depends on distillation quality

Paper: Qwen-VL: A Versatile Vision-Language Model for Understanding, Localization, Text Reading, and Beyond
Core idea: Extend a strong language model into a versatile VLM that handles image understanding, OCR, and localization tasks.
Known risks: complex data pipeline, visual grounding still needs careful evaluation

Paper: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
Core idea: Freezes pretrained weights and trains low-rank update matrices to adapt large models efficiently.
Known risks: rank choice sensitivity, adapter management complexity, not a full architecture search method alone
